In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new electrochemical and photochemical techniques for the study of the excited states of coordination complexes.
the synthesis and characterization of new luminescent coordination compounds.
the study of the chemistry of the transition metal—polypyridyl complexes.

chemiluminescence or electrochemilumnesence reactions involving metal-to-ligand charge transfer excited complexes are not a general phenomenon.

chemiluminescent and electrochemiluminiscent reactions involving coordination compounds are still in an early stage of development and that many interesting and useful results can be anticipated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chemiluminescence is a very useful tool for studying outer sphere electron transfer processes.

the electrochemilumnescence of the ruthenium complexes is not a simple one electron process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the comproportionation reaction can be viewed as a special case of outer—sphere redox reactions.
the electrochemilumnesence of coordination compounds is not a simple process and requires further study.
